fullPassage: When we read about psychology, how do we assess the quality of what we read? First, we cannot judge the quality of an argument on the basis of what it concludes about people, or on the basis of whether we agree with the author's beliefs about people or not. It is quite possible for two excellent psychologists to differ strongly about an aspect of human behaviour, while both providing convincing arguments and good evidence for reaching their conclusions. As you read more widely in psychology, you will find that there are many differences in opinion among researchers. It can even be the case that two researchers conduct what looks like the same experiment in two different settings, but get very different results. This does not mean, necessarily, that either of the researchers did bad work. On the contrary, different findings from different contexts may give us important information.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: differ → differences: 'many + 복수명사' 자리이므로 명사형
det.analysis: differ(동사, 다르다) → differences(명사, 차이). 'there are many ______ in opinion'에서 many 뒤에는 복수명사가 필요. 동사 differ를 명사 difference로 바꾸고 복수형 -s를 붙임
det.tip: differ(동사) → difference(명사) → differences(복수). many 뒤에는 복수명사

questions.passage: It is quite possible for two excellent psychologists to differ strongly about an aspect of human behaviour, while both providing __________ (convince) arguments and good evidence.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: convince → convincing: 명사 arguments를 앞에서 꾸미는 형용사(현재분사)
det.analysis: convince(동사, 설득하다) → convincing(현재분사/형용사, 설득력 있는). 뒤의 명사 arguments를 수식하여 '설득력 있는 논거'라는 능동의 의미를 만듦. 사람을 주어로 하면 convinced(설득된)이지만 여기서는 논거가 '설득하는' 쪽이므로 -ing 형태
det.tip: convince → convincing(설득력 있는, 능동) vs convinced(설득당한, 수동). 명사 앞 형용사 자리

questions.passage: When we read about psychology, how do we assess the quality of what we read? First, we cannot judge the quality of an argument on the basis of what it concludes about people, or on the basis of whether we agree with the author's beliefs about people or not. It is quite possible for two excellent psychologists to differ strongly about an aspect of __________, while both providing convincing arguments and good evidence for reaching their conclusions. As you read more widely in psychology, you will find that there are many differences in opinion among researchers. It can even be the case that two researchers conduct what looks like the same experiment in two different settings, but get very different results. This does not mean, necessarily, that either of the researchers did bad work. On the contrary, different findings from different contexts may give us important information.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 두 심리학자가 ______의 한 측면에 대해 강하게 의견을 달리하다
det.analysis:
✅ ① human behaviour(인간 행동): 심리학자들이 다루는 대상=인간 행동 ← 정답
❌ ② modern technology(현대 기술): 심리학의 주제와 거리가 멂
❌ ③ natural science(자연 과학): 심리학은 인간 행동을 다룸
❌ ④ global economy(세계 경제): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: psychology(심리학) → an aspect of human behaviour(인간 행동의 한 측면). 심리학의 연구 대상

questions.passage: When we read about psychology, how do we assess the quality of what we read? First, we cannot judge the quality of an argument on the basis of what it concludes about people, or on the basis of whether we agree with the author's beliefs about people or not. It is quite possible for two excellent psychologists to differ strongly about an aspect of human behaviour, while both providing convincing arguments and good evidence for reaching their conclusions. As you read more widely in psychology, you will find that there are many differences in opinion among researchers. It can even be the case that two researchers conduct what looks like the same experiment in two different settings, but get very different results. This does not mean, necessarily, that either of the researchers did bad work. On the contrary, different findings from different contexts may give us __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 서로 다른 맥락의 서로 다른 결과는 우리에게 ______을 줄 수 있다
det.analysis:
❌ ① misleading conclusions(오해를 주는 결론): 'On the contrary(오히려)'의 긍정 맥락과 모순
❌ ② identical results(동일한 결과): 앞에서 '서로 다른' 결과라 했으므로 모순
❌ ③ false evidence(거짓 증거): 부정적이라 긍정 맥락과 불일치
✅ ④ important information(중요한 정보): 서로 다른 결과가 '오히려' 중요한 정보를 준다 ← 정답
det.tip: This does not mean bad work. On the contrary(오히려) → 긍정적 결론. 서로 다른 결과의 가치=중요한 정보
